name: habit-pocket
description: Read, log and chart your Habit Pocket habits from ChatGPT.

interface.shortDescription: Log habits and see your stats
interface.longDescription:
Habit Pocket is a habit tracker that logs numbers, times of day and moods side by side, so you can see what your habits do to your sleep, mood and energy. This plugin lets ChatGPT work with your own Habit Pocket account.

Ask how your week is going and ChatGPT reads your habits, daily entries, streaks and completion rates, using the same numbers the app shows. Ask whether you sleep better on days you run, and it compares the two habits across the days you choose. Tell it what you did ("7.5 hours of sleep and meditation done for yesterday") and it logs the values, for one day or several. It can also create habits of any type (yes/no, number, time of day, or a list you define), add dashboard charts such as line, heatmap and candle, and rename or reorder your sections.

Limitations: ChatGPT can't delete or archive habits, change a habit's type, or edit a list habit's options. Those stay in the app, so nothing you've logged is lost or reinterpreted. It only sees the account you connect, habits filled from Garmin aren't available to it, and it doesn't set reminders.

Every change syncs to your iPhone and web app like any other entry. You sign in and approve access on a Habit Pocket consent page, and you can revoke it at any time. You need a Habit Pocket account to connect.
defaultPrompt: How's my week going? Anything I should worry about today?
Log 7.5 hours of sleep and mark meditation done for yesterday.
Do I sleep better on days I run? Check the last three months.

positive.description: Weekly review from the app's own stats
positive.prompt: How's my week going? Anything I should worry about today?
positive.expected_behavior: Sums up this week's completion rates and streaks with the app's numbers, and names streaks that end today if nothing is logged. No data changes.

positive.description: Logging values for a past day
positive.prompt: Log 7.5 hours of sleep and mark meditation done for yesterday.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolves yesterday in the account's timezone, saves 7.5 to Sleep hours and done to Meditation, and confirms both. The values show in the web app. If a day already had a value, it asks before overwriting.

positive.description: Comparing two habits over three months
positive.prompt: Do I sleep better on days I run? Check the last three months.
positive.expected_behavior: Gives average Sleep hours on run days and on other days, with the number of days in each group, and says it shows a pattern, not a cause.

positive.prompt: Start tracking water as a number in glasses, with a target of 8 a day.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates a number habit named Water with unit glasses, target 8 and goal at least, then confirms. It appears in the app's grid.

positive.prompt: Create a candle chart of my sleep window from bedtime to wake-up, overlaid with sleep hours.
positive.expected_behavior: Checks existing charts for a duplicate, then adds a candle chart with the previous day's Bedtime at the bottom, Wake-up on top and Sleep hours as the overlay.

negative.description: Deleting is not supported: there is no delete or archive tool, so ChatGPT should say it is done in the Habit Pocket app and call no write tool.
negative.prompt: Delete my Run habit and all of its history.

negative.description: Changing a habit's type is not supported, because it would reinterpret logged values. ChatGPT should point to the app or suggest creating a new number habit, leaving Mood unchanged.
negative.prompt: Change my Mood habit from a list to a number from 1 to 5.

negative.description: Out of scope: Habit Pocket has no reminders or notifications, so the plugin should not be called.
negative.prompt: Remind me at 7am tomorrow to go for a run.

review.commerce_description: The plugin does not sell anything or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: read habits, entries and stats; log and clear daily values; create habits and dashboard charts; rename and reorder sections.
